numerical_failure.observed_behavior: scipy.special.hankel2(0,0) returns (nan+nanj); the real part is NaN instead of 1. The reproducer scipy.special.jv(0,0) - 1j*scipy.special.yn(0,0) gives (nan+inf*j).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The original issue expects (1+nan*j), with real part 1 (jv(0,0)=1.0). A later discussion argues the real part should be NaN because it depends on the direction of approach to zero, and that nan+infj is the correct C99 complex infinity; the test added in the PR asserts np.isnan(res.real).
trigger_conditions: evaluated through scipy.special.hankel2 which dispatches to cyl_hankel_2 in scipy/special/xsf/bessel.h

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: z = 0 (exact zero), with H0^(2)(z) diverging logarithmically as z approaches 0; example values near zero are on the order of 1e-100 giving imaginary part about 146.66
category_specific_evidence: Issue #4517 reproducer: jv(0,0) - 1j*yn(0,0) returns (nan+inf*j); the second result (hankel2 at 0,0) is described as correct under C99 complex arithmetic where nan+infj is a representation of complex infinity.
Issue comment states the first result is not correctly given by the AMOS codes, which do not calculate non-finite results, and that overflow likely needs to be hardcoded.
DLMF 10.7.2 asymptotic: H0^(2)(z) ~ -(2i/pi) log z = -(2i/pi)[log|z| + i Arg(z)], so the real part depends on the direction of approach to zero.
Discussion reports hankel2(0, 1e-100) = 1+146.66092407099424j and hankel2(0, -1e-100) = 3+146.66092407099424j, and notes the asymptotic formula is missing a real-part offset of 1.
Merged patch special-cases v == 0 and z == 0 to return cy.real = NAN and cy.imag = INFINITY (the final test asserts np.isnan(res.real) and np.isposinf(res.imag)).

An intermediate suggestion set real part to 1.0 with imag INFINITY; a later test diff asserts res.real == 1, which conflicts with the final NaN real part, so the final expected value is the NaN/+inf form in the test_hankel2_gh4517 assertions.
reproduction_risks: Conflicting expected real part across passages: NaN (suggestion and final test) versus 1.0 (intermediate suggestion and a test variant).
Expected value depends on the chosen convention (C99 nan+infj versus the DLMF asymptotic); the PR body says the fix assumes the J_n/Y_n definition is appropriate.
Direction-dependent real part near zero (1 vs 3 at +/-1e-100) is not reconciled with the zero-argument special case.
Only exact input (0,0) is covered by the fix; other edge cases in related functions are explicitly stated as unfixed.
